title: A self-replicating artificial module-genome that generates bacterial chromosome replication system in vitro.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the full 12.6 MB supplementary archive. It contains exactly three items: 'DNA sequence.zip', 'Data_Fig4G_S2_Source_data.xlsx' (44.8 KB) and a 12.4 MB supplementary PDF. The sequence zip holds 25 real GenBank (.gbk) files (5 in SupTable1, 13 in SupTable2, 5 in SupTable3, 2 in SupTable4); the rest of its entries are macOS resource-fork stubs. I opened the largest, '1205_RCR module-genome v5.gbk': 53,137 bp circular synthetic construct with 35 annotated CDS (protein-coding) features. I opened both sheets of the spreadsheet in Python: they are gel band intensities for one figure panel plus one supplementary panel, 3 replicates x 3 replication rounds, with a pM (picomolar) standard curve, and 386 numeric cells in the whole workbook.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The claim of >28 doublings of recursive self-replication, the identity of the 26 RCR (Replication-Cycle Reaction) proteins, and the rescue-assay and expression-bottleneck results. Those results exist only as gel images and plots inside the supplementary PDF and the figures, not as any tabular file. I did not parse the 12.4 MB PDF page by page, but the Data Availability Statement itself lists only Supplementary Tables 1-5, GenBank sequences and figure source data as the complete data deposit.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplementary archive downloads freely from Europe PMC with no login; I unpacked it and read the files. No repository accession exists (no GEO, SRA, Zenodo or Dryad record found by paper_context.py).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. There is no prediction target column anywhere. The only outcome of interest ('does this construct self-replicate, and how well') exists as gel-electrophoresis images and plots inside a PDF; a label would have to be constructed by hand from figure panels for each of ~25 constructs.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present as literal sequence, not accessions: 25 GenBank files including the full 53,137 bp module-genome with 35 annotated coding sequences. Verified by reading the files.

a4_units_stated.note: The spreadsheet labels its columns 'Band Intensity of Sc (a.u.)' (arbitrary units) and 'pM' (picomolar), with a standard curve from 50 pM down. Units are stated; this is not where it fails.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified by counting. 25 GenBank constructs and 386 numeric cells in the entire source-data workbook (3 replicates x 3 rounds x 2 panels). The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification. This is three orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.3 MB of sequence plus a 45 KB spreadsheet
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; the whole supplement is 12.6 MB and 12.4 MB of that is a PDF of figures.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 53 kb module-genome claimed in the abstract is 53,137 bp in the deposited file 1205_RCR module-genome v5.gbk. Consistent, as far as there is anything to count.

a8_label_provenance.note: The few numbers that exist are physical measurements (densitometry of gel bands against a picomolar DNA standard curve), not another model's output. Provenance is clean; there is simply almost nothing of it.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available: with 25 engineered constructs and 386 measured numbers, any model would be fitting noise, and nothing it said would generalise beyond the handful of designs this one lab built.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA design of a synthetic gene cassette to predict whether it copies itself in a test tube.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one engineered DNA construct: its sequence, which genes it carries, how they are grouped into operons, their order and their ribosome binding sites. Verified count of deposited constructs: 25.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the construct self-replicates, and how much new DNA it makes. The true answer comes from running the reaction in a tube and measuring the supercoiled DNA band on a gel against a picomolar standard curve.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Bottom-up synthetic-cell labs currently find working genome designs by trial and error, so a design-to-function predictor would save months of cloning. But this paper cannot support one.

ml_idea: The only project this data suggests is predicting in-vitro self-replication from synthetic genome design (gene content, operon grouping, gene order, ribosome binding site strength). It is a genuinely interesting and uncrowded question, but it needs a design library of hundreds to thousands of constructs measured on one assay. This paper deposits 25 constructs and one quantitative panel. The data would have to come from a future combinatorial-design screen, not from here.

effort.compute_note: Sizes are measured, not estimated: the whole supplement is 12.6 MB on disk. No modelling estimates given because there is no trainable dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows. Unzipping the supplement and listing files takes two minutes and shows 25 GenBank constructs and 386 numeric cells, which kills it immediately.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A5 and A2, both verified by opening the files. This is a wet-lab milestone paper in bottom-up synthetic biology, not a dataset paper: the complete deposit is 25 GenBank sequence files for engineered plasmids and module-genomes, one spreadsheet with 386 numeric cells of gel band intensity (3 replicates x 3 replication rounds for two figure panels), and a 12.4 MB PDF of figures. There is no label column anywhere, and the outcome a model would predict (does this construct self-replicate) exists only as gel images that would have to be read out of a PDF by hand. Even if that were done, 25 constructs is far below the ~400-row floor for classification. The science is a real achievement; there is simply no machine-learning dataset attached to it.
